name: plaster
summary: Lime render on a wall: the pale, chalky, pitted stuff most of Lorencia's buildings are faced with.
why: Nothing in the library was a rendered wall. rock is a weathered boulder and flagstone is a
cut slab; plaster is neither - it is a soft coat troweled over masonry, and it fails in a
way stone does not, by pitting and flaking rather than by cracking along a plane.

Depth 0.06, down from 0.14 and then looked at again once the occlusion stopped drowning it. What MU paints on a render wall is dirt: dark speckles of staining, a few texels across, scattered over a pale ground. Read as height they become holes, and at 0.14 a house came out looking like pumice rather than plaster - every stain a pock with a shadow in it. This is the one material in the library where the art's luminance is *least* related to its relief, because the thing making it dark is on the surface rather than in it.
Roughness 0.90, just under grass. Lime render is about the most diffuse surface a town
has: it is chalk, and even wet it goes darker rather than shinier.
pitting and staining - millimetres of pock and a lot of colour - and MU's wall sheets have
a large luminance swing that is mostly dirt rather than relief. Pushed deeper the walls
came out looking like they had been shelled.
Range 0.12, high for something this uniform, because the difference between a dry wall and
the damp foot of one is most of what makes a rendered building look like it has stood
Cast, because render has no direction: it is floated on with a tool that goes every way.
